items.title: Scientists may have misread a 2-billion-year-old clue about Earth
items.title_en: Scientists may have misread a 2-billion-year-old clue about Earth
items.title_zh: 科学家们可能误读了一条关于地球的、距今20亿年的线索
items.summary_en: Scientists have found that a famous 2-billion-year-old chemical signature, once thought to record a massive global change in Earth’s carbon cycle, may instead have been produced by local magma, hydrocarbons, and methane-eating microbes. The discovery raises new questions about what was really happening as oxygen transformed the young planet.
items.summary_zh: 科学家发现，一种著名的、已有20亿年历史的化学特征——曾被认为记录了地球碳循环中的一次重大全球性变化——实际上可能是由局部岩浆、烃类物质以及以甲烷为食的微生物产生的。这一发现引发了新的疑问：当氧气改变这颗年轻行星的面貌时，当时究竟发生了什么。

items.summary_zh: 随着北极变暖和苔原解冻，长期被冻土封存的矿物质正渗入河流，使河水呈现橙色并变得呈酸性。阿拉斯加北部的一项研究发现，这种“生锈”的水比金属矿的排水更具金属味且酸度更高。在 E360 上阅读更多内容 →

items.title: Earth is tearing apart beneath the Pacific Northwest
items.title_en: Earth is tearing apart beneath the Pacific Northwest
items.title_zh: 太平洋西北地区地表之下，大地正在裂开
items.summary_en: Scientists have captured a subduction zone off Vancouver Island in the process of tearing itself apart, revealing that these massive tectonic systems may die piece by piece rather than all at once. The discovery could help explain ancient plate fragments, volcanic activity, and how hidden breaks beneath Cascadia may influence future earthquakes.
items.summary_zh: 科学家们捕捉到了温哥华岛外海一个正在自行分裂的俯冲带，这表明这些庞大的构造系统可能会一点一点地消亡，而不是一瞬间就消失。这一发现或许有助于解释古代板块碎片、火山活动，以及卡斯卡迪亚下方隐藏的断裂带如何影响未来的地震。
